SAMPLE SIZE.evidence_source: In addition to questionnaire measures, IQ was assessed for 174 participants who came in to the lab (119 female, 55 male).

ES.warning: No explicit correlation coefficient (Pearson r) between intelligence scores (WAIS-III) and creative achievement (CAQ) was found in the text.

Effects.evidence_source: No correlation coefficients between intelligence and creative achievement were found.

Mage.evidence_source: Participants included 245 individuals (169 females and 76 males), who ranged in age from 18 to 38 years (M 5 21.2, SD 5 3.1).

Measure IQ.evidence_source: Five WAIS-III subtests were used (Wechsler, 1997): vocabulary, similarities, block design, arithmetic, and digit-symbol coding.

IQ modality.evidence_source: Five WAIS-III subtests were used (Wechsler, 1997): vocabulary (verbal), similarities (verbal), block design (figural), arithmetic (verbal/performance), and digit-symbol coding (figural). Since both verbal and figural subtests were used, the modality is 'both'.

IQ Aspect.evidence_source: Ward and Ryan (1996) found this shortened version of the WAIS to afford a time savings of approximately 55% compared to the full WAIS, while maintaining a .97 correlation with full-scale IQ and a reliability coefficient of .96. Full-scale IQ measures general intelligence ('g').

Creativity Measures.evidence_source: All participants also completed the Creative Achievement Questionnaire (CAQ; Carson et al., 2005)

Domain classified.evidence_source: Points are awarded in each domain based on both level and number of concrete achievements, and the domains are summed to yield a total creative achievement score, which was transformed logarithmically to reduce skewness.

Number of studies.evidence_source: The section describes a single study's methodology, although it references 'Study 1' for some measures, implying this is a distinct study.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the methodology for a study involving 245 University of Toronto undergraduate students, with a mean age of 21.2 years. Participants completed various measures, including the Creative Achievement Questionnaire (CAQ) and five WAIS-III subtests for IQ assessment, administered to a subset of 174 participants. The text also mentions that some measures were administered "as in Study 1," indicating this is a separate study.
